civilopediaText.text: Roads have bridges over the rivers, and units move three times as fast on them.
Armies are supplied by their trains: units cost no gold upkeep.
An army's morale is not a city's: holding or capturing towns causes no unhappiness, so happiness stays level and there are no golden ages.
Both commanders have maps of the country: the whole terrain is revealed at the start, but enemy troops are only seen when your own units can see them. At night every unit sees one tile less.
Difficulty changes the fighting strength of computer-controlled armies: -15% on Recruit, -5% on Regular, normal on Veteran, +10% on Elite and +20% on Bloody Omaha.
